title: Citation-Consistent Voting for Permutation-Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation

contributions.purpose: Makes RAG systems robust to retrieved-document ordering (position bias) without any training.
contributions.mechanism: Citation-Consistent Voting (CCV): prompts the generator to cite supporting documents, filters responses for evidence validity, maps citations to permutation-invariant document IDs, and selects the answer with the highest citation-consistency score across multiple permutations, aggregating on document-ID agreement rather than answer frequency.
contributions.evaluation: On NaturalQuestions with Qwen3-8B and Contriever retrieval, CCV achieves 46.37% SubEM; requires no training and works with any RAG system producing structured citations.
contributions.source_quote: We propose Citation-Consistent Voting, a training-free inference-time method for permutation-robust RAG that exploits citation structure for answer aggregation.

contributions.purpose: Demonstrates that citation-based aggregation outperforms standard majority voting.
contributions.mechanism: Head-to-head comparison of CCV against answer-frequency majority voting across varying numbers of document permutations K.
contributions.evaluation: CCV improves SubEM by +0.19 points over majority voting on NaturalQuestions at K = 20 permutations, with gains scaling monotonically with K.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that CCV improves SubEM by +0.19 over majority voting on NaturalQuestions at K = 20 permutations, with gains scaling monotonically with K.

contributions.purpose: Establishes that citation consistency is a meaningful answer-quality signal.
contributions.mechanism: Diagnostic statistical analysis correlating document-ID agreement with answer correctness.
contributions.evaluation: Document-ID agreement correlates significantly with answer correctness (p = 1.14e-5).
contributions.source_quote: We validate that document-ID agreement correlates significantly with answer correctness (p = 1.14e-5), confirming that citation consistency is a meaningful quality signal.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our citation-consistent voting extends this paradigm by using document citations rather than answer frequency as the aggregation signal.
Our approach differs by exploiting the citation structure in model outputs, using document-ID agreement rather than answer frequency for aggregation, and requiring no training.

Inference-time methods like Mixture-of-Agents (Wang et al., 2024) generate multiple responses under different document orderings and aggregate via majority voting, but this approach ignores the rich citation structure that modern RAG systems produce.

notes: Headline improvement over majority voting is very small (+0.19 SubEM points at K=20), close to a tie; paper leans on monotonic scaling and the correlation diagnostic for support. Paper carries an automated-research-system generation warning.
